0.content:
Emilie named and invented her own profession. When the Maison Gardiennage closes a case, she shows her signed power-of-attorney papers and confidentiality agreement, steps over the cordon and restores the scene. Bodies and badly damaged objects have already been removed. She removes bloodstains, tissue and fragments with chemicals she adapted from test reagents. She asks nothing beyond the cleanup parameters, but from spatter, residue and how objects fell she can often piece together what happened. Afterwards she changes back into her own clothes in silence and nods to the clean room, feeling that part of the dead has only now been laid to rest.

She works as an independent contractor with a long-standing agreement with the Gardes and also takes private commissions. Occasionally the Maison asks her to help reconstruct a scene. She is discreet about the job because she handles sensitive information and protects her clients from unwanted attention. Relatives sometimes beg her not to erase the last traces of a loved one.

Neuvillette once recommended her to the Fortress of Meropide; Wriothesley declined, and Emilie suspects he wants some things left as a warning. Wriothesley says some things are best preserved "warts and all", the smell included. She wonders whether the water that washes away the remnants of the dead carries their resentment to the Fountain of Lucine.

1.content:
Emilie is the most famous perfume designer in Fontaine, works for no brand (not even the Confrerie of Cabriere), and calls perfumery her hobby. For her, perfume is close to a chemistry experiment and the perfumer bridges art and science. Once a perfume is sold, its meaning belongs to the wearer: Marcotte may smell like childhood to her and like love or regret to someone else. Her products sell out, with queues before dawn, while practical designs like insect-repellent perfume or a scent for Melusines never reach shop shelves.

She tests every product for shelf-life, works unscented, and grows or collects ingredients herself, sometimes at night. Chiori test-sells new samples in her boutique fitting room. Known creations include "Amber Wine" (an older perfume), "Yelena" (released after the 4.8 case) and a birthday fragrance of floral and fruity notes for the Traveler.

She has explored food-inspired fragrance design: a Boiled Fish perfume with Xiangling (6.4) and lessons in extraction for Escoffier. In the limited-time Homeward event (6.4) she made The Cat's Tail a Windwheel Aster fragrance, avoiding Cecilia because some cats dislike it.

2.content:
Emilie's 4.8 Story Quest. Nearly twenty years ago Fontaine's Perfume Mania drove "Auguste" to ten million Mora a bottle; its flower then vanished in a fire. Rumours of the flower reappearing in Sumeru and a wave of counterfeits compared to her work brought Emilie to a flower exhibition at Port Ormos. She hoped to puncture the myth. There she met the Traveler, cured Paimon's pollen sneezing, and reunited with her old teacher "Edgar", one of Auguste's creators, along with the merchant brothers Sylvain and Lucien, newly out of the Fortress of Meropide. "Edgar" was apparently attacked, Lucien died, and the truth emerged: the flower was grown by Yelena, an exiled Fatuus, with a Delusion that ruined her body, and she burned her garden and herself to hide the evidence.

Emilie realised that "Edgar" was Yelena's younger brother Kirya, who had used the Delusion to age himself, learned perfumery and taken Edgar's place. She suspects he killed the real Edgar. With Sheriff Shyam she faked Sylvain's death, swapped Kirya's "Auguste" for her own accord, and caught him when he drank it to die among his flowers. He survived, Eremites arrived, and he was held to stand trial. In the closing cinematic she declares: "Myths" can be deconstructed, "miracles" can be recreated.

Kirya killed with a Glaze Lily sealed shut with diluted Slime Condensate around an "Auguste" sample; it opened at night. Spirit Borneol incense made victims sensitive to its elemental energy. Emilie's accord used Rainbow Roses, Glaze Lilies and Cecilias, which once cancelled each other but can now be combined; Yelena had bred the flower to carry all three scents. Weeks later Emilie released "Yelena" and found that the three flowers' meanings combine into "Forget the past, and keep on living." Kirya said he could never forget his sister but thanked her for showing that Auguste could have meant something else.

3.content:
When Emilie's parents moved to Sumeru for work, the child Emilie studied perfumery basics under "Edgar", a Fontainian perfumer who had served a short sentence as an accomplice in the Auguste fraud and now only taught. He taught her that an accord can recreate scents that cannot be extracted, though "certain fragrances are simply one of a kind." Years later she learned he was Kirya, the young brother of the Fatuus Yelena, seeking revenge for her death. She stopped him and saved his life, and still called him "Master" to the end.

Kirya was unmoved by her findings: he could never forget his sister, and avenging her was "the meaning I chose for my life." He still thanked her for saving his life. Emilie visited him before his trial. She reflected that he had cultivated his revenge like a flower, and that she simply did not want to see any more death.

4.content:
Emilie and Chevreuse, captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, met through work, but their conversations are rarely serious. Chevreuse relies on Emilie's chemistry to identify a suspect's perfume, a bouquet's flowers or the soil on their boots, and says she has never been wrong. Chevreuse once called her unromantic. Emilie answered that perfumers who chase romance make bad perfume. Chevreuse loves crime novels mostly to argue about legal liability, and Emilie collects real news. Neither is the romantic one, and they think alike.

Chevreuse once told her about a novel in which a perfumer made the world's finest perfume from human tissue. From experience, Emilie doubts it would smell so wonderful; Chevreuse was busy working out who would be liable. In 6.7 both lent investigative and forensic expertise to a Fontinalia film.

5.content: Chiori, the designer, has a keen eye for trends and always picks the one of Emilie's test perfumes that will sell best. Under their business arrangement Emilie supplies small quantities of new perfumes to Chioriya Boutique; Eloffe sprays them in the fitting room, and Chiori passes on customer feedback. No customer has ever complained, and many ask where to buy the scent. Chiori buys a bottle herself whenever a release reaches the shops. Visiting Emilie's spotless home, she asked bluntly whether it was some kind of compulsion; Emilie laughed: "It has to be this way, that's all."

6.comment: Emilie: Neuvillette and the secret of Fontainians
6.content: Through cleanup work Emilie noticed minuscule differences between Fontainian human tissue and that of other nations, which most people blamed on Fontaine's environment. After the prophecy was fulfilled, the differences vanished. She visited Iudex Neuvillette, who had reportedly explained Fontainians' origins at the Opera Epiclese, and he said, "Fontainians are now true humans." That was enough for her; she sensed the details were a threshold ordinary people should not cross, and she keeps the secret locked away. She also once attended his water-tasting; his sincere, abstract descriptions reminded her of perfume reviews, and she still buys the waters he recommended.

7.content: Her father is a Marechaussee Phantom officer and her mother a forensic pathologist and perfume enthusiast. Emilie often has dinner at their home, where human and Melusine colleagues are frequent guests. Melusines helped look after her as a baby, and Sigewinne met her then, though Emilie was too young to remember. Sigewinne never treats her as a junior, praises her perfumes and plans to buy armfuls for the girls at the Fortress. Emilie sets aside a sample of each new perfume for her. Many of the perfumes in Emilie's collection were gifts from her mother.

8.content: Emilie usually arrives after a case is closed, when only a guard remains. Once, a dazed young woman, kin of the victim, was pacing the cordon, unable to leave. Emilie could have simply shown her papers and gone in. Instead she sat with the woman for hours, holding her hand while she talked about the deceased, until only quiet sorrow remained. Packing up late in the dim light, she saw the Vision glimmering. From then on she never set time limits on her work, so she could always listen.

9.content: Charlotte, reporter for The Steambird, uncovered the true nature of Emilie's work and chose not to publish it, against her own professional interest. Emilie respects her highly and would not refuse her help. Charlotte raves about Emilie's insect-repellent, anti-perspirant perfume. Emilie first heard of the Traveler through The Steambird. In 6.7 Emilie acted with Charlotte's crew in a detective film.

10.content: Tighnari found her address by roundabout means and wrote asking for her flower expertise. She asked about Sumerian perfume ingredients in return, and they became casual pen pals; he tells her about his companions. At Port Ormos he vouched for her expertise and helped with the case, and she met his apprentice Collei. When Collei sympathised with Kirya, Emilie told her that empathy is human but must not cloud judgment, and that a single act of vengeance can put the answers out of reach forever.

11.comment: Emilie: Escoffier, Xiangling and food fragrances
11.content: Escoffier, a studious chef, learned fragrance extraction from Emilie and does not fall asleep at dry perfumery lectures. Emilie credits her success to diligence, not natural gift. In the anecdote "Emilie: Alternative Uses" (6.4), Emilie visited Liyue Harbor and, with Xiangling's help, made a perfume that smelled exactly like Wanmin Restaurant's Boiled Fish. Hu Tao proposed scented menus, then borrowed the bottle to spritz Zhongli's Almond Tofu as a prank. Emilie's view: creations made on a whim are for pleasure, so use them wherever inspiration strikes.

12.content: During the limited-time Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind event (6.4), Emilie came to Mondstadt on business. A woman calling herself a mage (Alice) had her manage a flower shop full of rare plants in exchange for studying them; in Alice's bubble-magic recreation of Mondstadt, the shop's non-local flowers were one of the "discrepancies". The Cat's Tail commissioned a house fragrance. Her first Valberry trial was so sweet that the bartender fell asleep, so she switched to Windwheel Aster. At the Traveler's drinks stand she asked for a Lumidouce Twilight variant with more depth. She said she avoids sugary food, drinks fruit tea after work with Maison Gardiennage friends, and likes only light alcohol. She named the Traveler's finished drink, a Windwheel Aster take on the Lumidouce Twilight, the "Windborne Bouquet".

13.content: In the 6.7 Story Quest Sunny Summer Fontinalia, Emilie played "Jacoba" in the detective film shot by Charlotte's crew under director Lepine-Pauline, opposite Charlotte as "Hurlock" and Navia as "Gina". The shoot took place in an aquarium. She and Chevreuse advised on criminal investigation and forensics, which Clorinde credited for the film's realism. Emilie later attended the wrap celebration with Chevreuse, Chiori, Clorinde and Navia. The story quest stays available after the event.

14.content: Clorinde has heard of Emilie's real profession; once they passed each other on the street while Emilie was smiling and petting a small dog, and they simply nodded. Emilie finds the duelist easy to talk to. Wriothesley turned down her services for the Fortress of Meropide without ever meeting her. Lyney liked her perfumes, but Lynette's tail vetoed a purchase; Lynette, sensitive to perfume and reluctant to sneeze rudely, takes the long way round the queues.
